description: The Pro degassing estimate (research/degassing/PLAN.md): how many days an XLPE core stays in the oven until a share of its crosslinking by-product is left, by Fick diffusion with published coefficients (Polymers 11 (2019) 1439; the methane D0 and Ea of IEEE PES T&D 2016 as quoted there; Electric Wire & Cable 2025 at 65 C), never a standard's result: no standard gives a degassing formula, time or residual limit. The answer is a band (an open conductor with the 2025 coefficient to a sealed conductor with the 2016 one), the cases at 50, 20, 10 and 5 % left, the curve, the highest local share, the time at 60, 65, 70 and 80 C, each step with its source and seen level, the notes and the warnings (drum turns, sheath, uniform start, no chemistry). For MV (up to 46 kV) the AEIC CS8-20 cl. 10.2 wait is given beside it as the standard's printed value (cs8), with the model's residual at its conditions. A factory measurement (input.calibration) fits an effective coefficient and replaces the band. Always paid, at its own price: on the site a member's calculation with no free part. input: {tempC? (oven, 20 to 80, default 70; warned above 70), target? (share of the start left, 0.01 to 0.9, default 0.1), byproduct?: methane | polar (polar indicative), compound?: standard | low (low by-product: half the start), heatupH? (drum heat-up, h, a ramp from 20 C; default 0), startPpm? and targetPpm? (both or neither), calibration?: {tempC, days, residual (share left, GC), boundary?: sealed | open, heatupH?, conductorMm? and systemMm? (the measured cable; absent: this design)}}. $5.00 per calculation in USDC with x402; no free allowance; a list of up to 50 items at $5.00 per item, one payment.
